predecessors.note: Cliopatria starts the emirate in 830; the Byzantine Empire dossier records the loss of Crete in 827.

land.text: the whole island, retaken by Nikephoros Phokas: Chandax stormed 6 March 961, 'the rest of Crete quickly capitulated'; it became a Byzantine theme with its strategos at Chandax

capitals.name: Chandax (al-Khandaq, Heraklion)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Chandax, 'their main city and fortress'; the page says the capital moved from Gortyn to Chandax without dating the move, so Chandax is given for the whole life.

correction.text: shape unchanged (the island of Crete), but held from the landing of 827 (the page: 'either 824 or 827/828'; 'usually dated to 827 or 828') to 959

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria starts 830. The page gives no area, so the 5,499 km2 of the shape cannot be compared; the shape's bbox (23.6-26.2 E, 35.0-35.5 N) spans the island's length, and the page says Abu Hafs 'slowly consolidated control of the entire island', so the island is the right unit, with the Greek countryside 'left relatively alone' in the mountains. The 842-843 Byzantine occupation of 'much of the island' (contest events) is not drawn in the Cliopatria shape.

correction.text: shape unchanged, but it holds until Chandax is stormed on 6 March 961 (Phokas landed in June or July 960 and besieged Chandax over the winter)

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria's single year 960 stops a year short; 'The campaign lasted from autumn 960 until spring 961' and the Byzantines took Chandax on 6 March 961, after which 'The rest of Crete quickly capitulated'. The Byzantine Empire dossier gains Crete in 961.

region.text: Crete, the island won from the Byzantine Empire by the Andalusian exiles

ledger.note: 827: Andalusian exiles take Crete and found the emirate. 'A group of Arab Andalusian exiles led by Abu Hafs Umar al-Iqritishi conquered Crete in either 824 or 827/828'; 'usually dated to 827 or 828' (Muslim sources), c. 824 for Christides and Makrypoulias (Byzantine sources). They made Chandax their 'main city and fortress' and Abu Hafs 'slowly consolidated control of the entire island'; the page dates neither the founding of Chandax nor the end of the consolidation, so the whole island is given from the start.

region.text: much of the island, occupied by Theoktistos' army

ledger.note: 842: Theoktistos lands an imperial army on Crete. Under Theoktistos the army 'succeeded in occupying much of the island' (the page's heading gives 842-843); the Chandax page: the Byzantines recovered 'parts of the island in 842-843 ... Those gains were lost'.

843: Theoktistos withdraws, the garrison is cut down. He 'withdrew for political reasons, and the troops left behind were slaughtered by the Arabs'; the reconquest 'was not completed'. The emirate holds the whole island again.

region.text: Crete, the countryside and the siege of Chandax

ledger.note: 960: Nikephoros Phokas lands on Crete. He 'sailed in June or July 960, landed on the island, and defeated the initial Muslim resistance' (Emirate page); the campaign 'lasted from autumn 960 until spring 961' (Chandax page); the Muslims fled into Chandax. The page gives June or July, so no month is entered.

961: Chandax is stormed. 'On 6 March, the Muslims were routed and fled back into the streets'; soldiers took 'the traditional three days of plunder'; the emir Abd al-Aziz and his son were taken prisoner.

961: the Emirate of Crete falls to Byzantium. 'The rest of Crete quickly capitulated to the Byzantine army' and the island became a theme with its strategos based at Chandax, after 134 years of Muslim rule (Emirate page: 'from the late 820s to the reconquest ... in 961').

wars.name: Byzantine attempts to retake Crete under Michael II
wars.outcome: Failure: the expedition of Photeinos and Damian was defeated and Damian killed, Krateros' was routed and he was executed; Ooryphas drove the Arabs from the Aegean islands but 'failed to retake Crete'. The Arabs destroyed an imperial fleet off Thasos in October 829.
wars.note: Dated c. 824-829 under Michael II on the page; no border moved.

wars.name: Theoktistos' expedition to Crete

zones.text: much of the island, occupied by Theoktistos' army and then lost

wars.outcome: Theoktistos 'succeeded in occupying much of the island' but withdrew for political reasons; the troops left behind were slaughtered and the reconquest 'was not completed'.
wars.note: The Chandax page confirms a strategos of Crete in the Taktikon Uspensky for these years. Later failed expeditions: 866 (Bardas assassinated before the campaign), 911 (Himerios, 177 ships) and 949 (Constantine Gongyles, 128 ships, 'routed in a surprise attack'): no ground held, no contest events.

wars.name: Siege of Chandax (Byzantine reconquest of Crete)

zones.text: Crete, from the landing of 960 to the storming of Chandax on 6 March 961

wars.outcome: Byzantine victory: Chandax stormed on 6 March 961, the last emir Abd al-Aziz captured, the island a Byzantine theme.
wars.note: Phokas destroyed an Arab relief army (Leo the Deacon: about 40,000) and used miners and a feinted battering ram in the March assault.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the border, but the pages give no survey, the Greek mountain communities were 'left relatively alone', and the Aegean islands that reportedly paid jizya to Crete (Aegina, Elafonisos, Cythera, Naxos, 'could well be longer') are undated and not drawn.

notes: Within the 1-2 page budget (two pages). Conquest date: 'either 824 or 827/828' on the page; 827 used because the Byzantine Empire dossier (loss, 827) and Cliopatria (830) are near it. Dependencies not drawn: the Aegean islands said to pay jizya to Crete (Aegina, Elafonisos, Cythera, Naxos) and the possible occupation of Athens c. 896-902 (page says 'may have been') have no dates and no region sure enough to enter as events; the raids on Euboea (c. 835-840) and Lesbos (837) are raids, not holdings. Nominal suzerainty: 'De facto independent, nominally under suzerainty of the Abbasid Caliphate' (infobox); the page's phrase for the origin, 'Abbasid vassals', is not used for the conquest, which the Andalusians made as exiles expelled from Alexandria. No vassal event is entered; the Abbasid Caliphate dossier (af-02 / me group) may carry a nominal tint. Chandax: founding date not given on either page. No gazetteer names are needed (Crete resolves).
